title: Cobra Effect Lab
one_liner: Design an incentive, then watch an animated population simulation backfire exactly like the podcast's historical disasters.
speaker: Peter Diamandis
context: Peter recounts how a French bounty on rat tails in Hanoi led to rat farming, and Wells Fargo's account-opening quota led employees to create 3.5 million fake accounts.
demo: User picks a scenario (rat bounty, sales quota, arrest quota) and sets a reward dial. An animated bar/population chart runs forward in simulated weeks, showing the 'intended metric' rising nicely while a hidden 'real outcome' metric (actual rats killed, real new customers, real criminals caught) stagnates or drops, revealing the gaming strategy that emerged. A final screen shows the real historical numbers from the episode.
data_plan: Bundled dataset of the three real anecdotes' facts from the transcript (rat tail bounty, Wells Fargo 3.5M fake accounts, ICE arrest quotas) plus a simple labeled simulated agent-behavior model for the interactive chart.
risks: The ICE example is politically charged; keep framing strictly on the incentive-design mechanic and the historical rat/bank examples to avoid partisan framing.

episode.title: Flying Tesla Car, Robot Brains Halving in Cost Every 3 Weeks, and Why Incentives Decide AI Alignment | #303
